## 318553: extremal pebbling, two sustained routes

Read 0905.3949v2 definitions pp2–6 and Section2.5 pp16–17, including Conjecture2.21, both parity constructions and Proposition2.20 proof. For d=2k, G_n,d is a spider with floor((n-1)/k) arms of length k and one residual arm. For d=2k+1 it is a clique of floor(n/(k+1)) vertices each with a pendant k-path and an optional residual path. The integer constraints for an actually feasible diameter must be retained; the source's phrase 'all n,d' does not make impossible order/diameter pairs meaningful.

Route A: shortest-path tree bound. At a root r choose a breadth-first spanning tree. Each rooted path-partition length a_i is at most d, and sum a_i=n-1. The source's Chung input gives pi(T,r)=1+sum(2^a_i-1). Since (2^a-1)/a is increasing, pi(G,r)<=1+(2^d-1)(n-1)/d. The inequality follows directly by multiplying each a_i by the largest allowable slope and summing. This does not approach the target extremal slope (2^ceil(d/2)-1)/ceil(d/2). In particular for d=4 the two slopes are 15/4 and 3/2. No amount of floor rounding closes this linear gap.

Stronger tree restriction investigated: after choosing a longest root-directed path of length e in a tree of diameter 2k, a branch departing at depth t has height b satisfying b<=e-t (maximality) and b<=2k-e+t (distance to the far endpoint). Adding yields b<=k. Hence all subsequent paths in a greedy rooted partition have length <=k. Conditional on the exact Chung rooted-maximal-partition theorem quoted by the source, convex transfer of units into the largest part, then into parts of capacity k, gives the extremal sequence (2k,k,...,k,r), sum n-1, 0<=r<k. Its value is 2^(2k)+q(2^k-1)+(2^r-1), q=floor((n-1-2k)/k). This is the source spider value. The transfer inequality is (2^(a+1)-1)+(2^(b-1)-1)>=(2^a-1)+(2^b-1) for a>=b>=1. Zero parts are discarded. This is a TREE subcase, not the target all-graph theorem, and the Chung input is attributed rather than freshly audited from its original paper.

Why this fails for graphs: a BFS tree preserves distances to r but not distances between two branch endpoints. Their tree distance may exceed 2k even though an off-tree shortcut makes their graph distance <=2k. Thus b<=2k-e+t is no longer justified in that tree. The exact unpaid lemma is a shortcut-sensitive replacement of the path partition, with no larger total exponential cost and with only one long part. Simply calling the graph diameter a tree diameter is false.

Route B: try to violate the bound using several heavy branches joined through a small diameter-two core. The source's odd construction already realizes the clique-core mechanism; it cannot itself be a new counterexample. ## 376921: cut-free self-dual realization, two mechanisms

Read math/0003172v3 Section6 pp15–18, Theorems6.1–6.2, Conjecture6.1 and the checkerboard/spanning-tree proof text. The intended statement is EXISTENCE of some graph for each eligible odd n. Their knot-theoretic inputs are attributed; the material tangle drawings were not visually checked, so I do not claim a new independent audit of these constructions.

Route A: multiply known self-dual realizations. A one-vertex join preserves planar realizability and multiplies spanning-tree counts: a spanning tree restricts to a spanning tree in each block, since the only connection is the shared vertex, and conversely the union of the two block trees is a tree. But that shared vertex is a cut vertex as soon as both blocks have other vertices. Consequently factoring n=g^2*m and combining a square realization with a primitive one does not solve the target. A two-terminal gluing might repair connectivity, but its tree count includes both tree and separating-forest terms; multiplication alone is not the count. The unpaid lemma is an explicit cut-free self-dual two-terminal operation with controlled tree/forest pair and exact norm multiplication, for all necessary prime-power factors. No such operation was derived.

Route B: use cyclic symmetry instead of block multiplication. A wheel with four rim vertices is self-dual: the outer face and center exchange roles, while the four triangular faces correspond cyclically to the four rim vertices. Removing the center leaves a cycle; removing a rim vertex leaves a connected graph through the center. Thus it has no cut vertex. Its reduced Laplacian on the rim is 3I-A(C4). The constant vector, alternating vector, and two independent opposite-difference vectors have eigenvalues1,5,3,3, so the matrix-tree theorem gives45 spanning trees. This supplies a useful check: a nonprimitive representation 45=3^2+6^2 is realizable; nonprimitivity is not itself an obstruction. Neither the wheel mechanism nor block multiplication yields every eligible nonsquare. The missing theorem must handle all such n and exclude the three exceptional values with the source's exact planar/multigraph conventions. No all-parameter construction or forbidden admissible n was proved. PARK. A small full witness could have been significant; this exclusion is instead because the universal existence quantifier remains unpaid.
